text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Shin Bet chief Ayalon weighed resignation because of ties with Prime Minister Netanyahu; decided not to shake up agency.
- Jordan: 'settlements endanger our security'. United States: they're an obstacle to peace.
- Security apparatus ready to free Soviet spy Klingberg on limited conditions.
- Palestinian Authority denies report that instigators of Beit-El attack sentenced to 25 years in prison.
- Rabbinate blocks Moslem conversions because it has not found security official to approve them.
- Scitex workers propose purchasing activities from company, management refuses.
- Deputy Housing Minister Porush: forbid sale of state lands to companies registered overseas.
- Treasury plans to close four appraisal offices.
JERUSALEM POST
- Clinton slams settlement policy.
- Monitoring panel: Lebanon responsible for Katyusha attack.
- Official 1997 inflation target set at 7-10 percent.
- Shekem to sell its food business to Super-Sol.
- Mutual fund management company Ilanot, Batucha Securities and Investments complete merger.
- Bezeq may install integrated service digital network (ISDN) lines in all new homes.
- Finance Minister Meridor: Plan for competition in car insurance market by March.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Clinton: settlements an obstacle to peace.
- Senior security officials: 'we are worried about government decision making procedures'.
MAARIV
- Ayalon weighed resignation but decided not to for the good of the organisation.
- Poll: 22 percent would not enlist if army service was voluntary.
GLOBES
- 1997 Inflation target 7-10 percent; 1998 target possible.
- Bank of Israel likely to lower interest some 0.5 percent.
- Netanyahu and Meridor: compromise on budget reached, additional changes after Knesset approval.
